goi-cu-hu-dua-tom-thit-ben-tre.name: Ben Tre Coconut Heart Salad with Shrimp and Pork
aliases: Young coconut heart salad with shrimp and pork
goi-cu-hu-dua-tom-thit-ben-tre.serving_basis: A shared salad for four people.
goi-cu-hu-dua-tom-thit-ben-tre.description: Crisp young coconut heart is tossed with shrimp, pork belly, Vietnamese coriander and a sweet-sour fish-sauce dressing. Bếp Việt keeps the dressing light so the fresh ingredients remain the focus.
goi-cu-hu-dua-tom-thit-ben-tre.finished_dish: The coconut heart stays crisp, the shrimp is just cooked and the pork is tender; the balanced dressing lightly coats the ingredients.
goi-cu-hu-dua-tom-thit-ben-tre.serving: Toss shortly before serving and finish with roasted peanuts and fried shallots. Serve with shrimp crackers or toasted rice paper as an appetizer.
tips: Soak sliced coconut heart briefly in cool water with a little lime to preserve its color, then drain thoroughly.
Poach the shrimp until just pink and cook the pork through; cool both before tossing so the herbs stay fresh.
Mix the dressing separately and add gradually to keep the salad balanced and crisp.
search_terms: Ben Tre coconut heart shrimp pork salad
goi-cu-hu-dua-tom-thit-ben-tre.image_alt: A Vietnamese coconut heart salad with poached shrimp, pork belly, carrot, Vietnamese coriander, peanuts and fried shallots on a transparent background.
goi-cu-hu-dua-tom-thit-ben-tre.time_note: About 50 minutes; poaching time depends on the size of the shrimp and pork, which should be fully cooked before cooling.

ingredients.name: Young coconut heart
ingredients.notes: Finely shred; soak briefly in cool lemon water and drain well.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Part may be replaced with rice vinegar.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For poaching the pork and shrimp.

preparation_steps: Rinse the shrimp, pork and herbs separately. Shred the coconut heart, briefly soak in diluted lime water and drain; cut the carrot and coriander.
Bring lightly salted water to a boil and poach the pork until fully cooked. Cool, then slice thinly.
Poach the shrimp just until pink and opaque; cool and peel if desired.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice and sugar until dissolved; add garlic and chili, then adjust the balance.
cooking_steps: Combine the coconut heart, carrot, pork and shrimp in a large bowl. Add the dressing gradually and toss gently.
Let stand for 5–7 minutes, fold in the Vietnamese coriander and toss once more; drain excess liquid if needed.
Arrange on a serving plate and finish with roasted peanuts and fried shallots just before serving.
goi-cu-hu-dua-tom-thit-ben-tre.media_alt_text: A Ben Tre coconut heart salad with poached shrimp, pork belly, carrot, Vietnamese coriander, peanuts and fried shallots on a transparent background.

ca-thoi-loi-nuong-muoi-ot-ca-mau.name: Ca Mau Grilled Mudskipper with Chili Salt
ca-thoi-loi-nuong-muoi-ot-ca-mau.description: Ca Mau mudskipper is cleaned, seasoned with chili salt and grilled until fragrant and just cooked. Bếp Việt keeps the seasoning simple and serves the fish with herbs, cucumber and lime.
ca-thoi-loi-nuong-muoi-ot-ca-mau.finished_dish: The skin is fragrant and lightly charred, the flesh stays moist and opaque, and the chili-salt coating is savory with moderate heat.
ca-thoi-loi-nuong-muoi-ot-ca-mau.serving: Pull the fish while hot and eat with herbs, cucumber and chili-lime salt. Serve with steamed rice or wrap in rice paper.
tips: Choose fresh fish and clean away mud and slime thoroughly; drain well before seasoning.
Score the fish lightly so the seasoning spreads evenly; keep the marinating time short to avoid drawing out moisture.
Grill over glowing charcoal or in a preheated oven; turn carefully and check that the thickest part is fully opaque.
search_terms: Ca Mau grilled mudskipper chili salt
ca-thoi-loi-nuong-muoi-ot-ca-mau.image_alt: Ca Mau mudskipper grilled with chili salt on an oval plate with cucumber, herbs and lime, isolated on a transparent background.
ca-thoi-loi-nuong-muoi-ot-ca-mau.time_note: About 65 minutes including marinating; grill until the flesh is opaque through the thickest section.

ingredients.name: Mudskipper fish
ingredients.notes: Clean thoroughly, remove gills and entrails, then drain.

ingredients.name: Red chilies
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the preferred heat level.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and pound with the chili and salt.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Brush lightly on the fish to prevent sticking.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Add a small pinch to the marinade.

preparation_steps: Rinse the fish several times, remove mud, gills and entrails, gently scrape away slime, rinse again and pat dry.
Make a few shallow slashes on both sides so the seasoning reaches the flesh.
Pound the salt, chilies and garlic; mix with lime juice, pepper and oil into a coarse paste. Marinate the fish for about 15 minutes.
Trim and wash the herbs and cucumber, then drain. Prepare the charcoal grill or preheat the oven.
cooking_steps: Preheat a grill or oven to about 200°C. Lightly oil the grate and arrange the fish.
Grill for about 8–12 minutes per side depending on size, turning gently once; brush with a little marinade if the surface dries.
Check the thickest part: the fish is done when the flesh is opaque throughout and separates easily from the bone. Transfer to a plate.
Serve hot with herbs, cucumber, lime and rice or rice paper.
ca-thoi-loi-nuong-muoi-ot-ca-mau.media_alt_text: Ca Mau mudskipper grilled with chili salt, served with cucumber, herbs and lime; the skin is lightly charred and golden.

banh-hoi-bo-dun-ben-tre.name: Ben Tre Grilled Beef Rolls with Fine Woven Rice Vermicelli
aliases: Fine woven rice vermicelli with grilled beef rolls
Grilled beef rolls served with Vietnamese woven rice noodles
banh-hoi-bo-dun-ben-tre.serving_basis: A shared meal for four people.
banh-hoi-bo-dun-ben-tre.description: Soft fine woven rice vermicelli brushed with scallion oil is served with charcoal-grilled beef rolls filled with pork fat, Chinese sausage and peanuts. Pineapple, sour starfruit, green banana, herbs and sweet-sour fish sauce complete the familiar Ben Tre meal.
banh-hoi-bo-dun-ben-tre.finished_dish: The beef rolls are fragrant and lightly charred with a rich but balanced filling; soft vermicelli, scallion oil and tart fruit keep the meal in balance.
banh-hoi-bo-dun-ben-tre.serving: Arrange the vermicelli and grilled beef separately with herbs, pineapple, starfruit, green banana and dipping sauce. Wrap each bite or mix on the plate.
tips: Slice the beef across the grain and thinly so it cooks quickly in the roll.
Do not overfill with pork fat, sausage and peanuts or the rolls may open on the grill.
Grill until the beef is fully cooked; use separate tongs and plates for raw and cooked meat.
dish_type: Grilled beef rolls with fine woven rice vermicelli
search_terms: Ben Tre grilled beef rolls with fine woven rice vermicelli
grilled beef rolls with Vietnamese woven rice noodles
Ben Tre beef and noodle platter
banh-hoi-bo-dun-ben-tre.image_alt: Fine woven rice vermicelli brushed with scallion oil, served with grilled beef rolls filled with sausage, pork fat and peanuts, fresh herbs and dipping sauce on a transparent background.
banh-hoi-bo-dun-ben-tre.time_note: About 85 minutes; grilling time varies with roll thickness, and the beef should be cooked through.

ingredients.name: Fine woven rice vermicelli
ingredients.notes: Use fresh, soft woven rice vermicelli and warm it before serving.

ingredients.name: Pork fat
ingredients.notes: Cut into small pieces for the rolls.

ingredients.name: Chinese sausage
ingredients.notes: Steam, lightly brown in a pan and cut into strips.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Finely mince for the beef marinade.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Finely mince for the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Green cooking banana
ingredients.notes: Slice, briefly soak in salted water and drain.

preparation_steps: Slice the beef across the grain. Boil the pork fat until cooked, cool and dice; steam the Chinese sausage, lightly brown it in a pan and cut into strips.
Marinate the beef with shallot, some fish sauce, sugar and pepper for about 15 minutes.
Wash and drain the herbs; peel and slice the pineapple, starfruit and green banana. Briefly soak the banana in lightly salted water to limit browning, then drain.
Finely slice the scallions. Stir the fish sauce, lime, sugar, garlic, chili and warm water into a sweet-sour dipping sauce.
cooking_steps: Wrap each beef slice around a little pork fat, Chinese sausage and peanut; secure with a toothpick or place seam-side down.
Grill over glowing charcoal or in a grill pan over medium heat, turning until the beef is fully cooked and lightly charred.
Warm the fine woven rice vermicelli according to package directions. Heat the oil gently, turn off the heat, stir in the scallions to make scallion oil and brush it over the vermicelli.
Serve the grilled beef with fine woven rice vermicelli, herbs, pineapple, starfruit, green banana and dipping sauce.
banh-hoi-bo-dun-ben-tre.media_alt_text: Fine woven rice vermicelli brushed with scallion oil, served with grilled beef rolls filled with Chinese sausage, pork fat and peanuts, fresh produce and dipping sauce.

buoi-da-xanh-ben-tre.name: Ben Tre Green-Skin Pomelo Dessert
buoi-da-xanh-ben-tre.serving_basis: One pomelo, separated into four portions.
buoi-da-xanh-ben-tre.description: Ben Tre green-skin pomelo is peeled and served by itself as a light fruit course, without mixing it with other fruit or sauce. Its pink, relatively dry flesh and clean sweetness make a refreshing finish to a family meal.
buoi-da-xanh-ben-tre.finished_dish: The segments remain whole and plump, with a clean, lightly sweet flavor and no bitter or pithy aftertaste; serve cool, not ice-cold.
buoi-da-xanh-ben-tre.serving: Separate the segments, remove any seeds and arrange on a chilled plate. Serve individually after the meal without added sugar or other fruit.
tips: Wash the rind before cutting so the knife does not carry dirt to the flesh.
Remove the thick white pith and separate the membrane gently to keep the juice vesicles intact.
Chill briefly; do not soak the segments in water, which would dilute their naturally dry texture.
buoi-da-xanh-ben-tre.image_alt: A whole Ben Tre green-skin pomelo beside a plate containing only its pink segments, isolated on a transparent background.
buoi-da-xanh-ben-tre.time_note: About 35 minutes including brief chilling; no cooking is needed, and the fruit is served on its own after a meal.
suggested_pairings: Serve by itself after a family meal

ingredients.name: Green-skin pomelo from Ben Tre
ingredients.notes: Choose a ripe, firm fruit with intact green or yellow-green skin.

preparation_steps: Wash and dry the whole fruit before cutting.
Trim both ends, score the rind along the lobes and peel away the thick white pith.
Separate the segments gently, remove any seeds and keep the vesicles intact.
cooking_steps: No cooking is needed. Arrange the pomelo segments on a clean plate, chill briefly and serve by itself after the meal.
buoi-da-xanh-ben-tre.media_alt_text: A whole green-skin pomelo from Ben Tre beside a plate of pink pomelo segments only, on a transparent background.

tep-rang-dua-ben-tre.name: Ben Tre Coconut-Braised Silver Shrimp
aliases: Silver shrimp braised in coconut cream
Mekong Delta shrimp cooked with coconut milk
tep-rang-dua-ben-tre.serving_basis: A shared savory dish for four people.
tep-rang-dua-ben-tre.description: Fresh silver shrimp are quickly cooked in first-press coconut cream until orange-red and lightly glazed. This everyday dish from Ben Tre is served with steamed rice; Bếp Việt edits the seasoning for a home-size portion.
tep-rang-dua-ben-tre.finished_dish: The shrimp are orange-red and hold their shape beneath a light coconut glaze, with balanced natural sweetness and coconut richness.
tep-rang-dua-ben-tre.serving: Serve hot on a small platter with steamed rice and blanched vegetables or a light soup.
tips: Choose very fresh, soft-shelled shrimp and drain them well so the pan sauce does not become watery.
Wait for the coconut cream to boil before adding shrimp; lower the heat only after they turn orange-red so they stay firm.
Toss gently and stop when the sauce forms a light glossy coating; overcooking can make the shrimp dry or soft.
search_terms: silver shrimp braised in coconut cream
tep-rang-dua-ben-tre.image_alt: A plate of orange-red freshwater shrimp cooked in coconut cream, lightly glazed, on a transparent background.
tep-rang-dua-ben-tre.time_note: About 35 minutes; cooking time varies with shrimp size and pan width.

ingredients.name: Fresh silver freshwater shrimp
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh shrimp; keep the shells on.

ingredients.name: First-press coconut cream
ingredients.notes: Use the thick first extraction for fragrance and richness.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the natural sweetness of the shrimp.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use sparingly to balance the coconut richness.

preparation_steps: Pick out any spoiled shrimp, rinse quickly and drain thoroughly. Trim sharp antennae from larger shrimp if desired; keep the shells on so they retain their shape and color.
Measure the first-press coconut cream and prepare the sugar and salt. Use a wide pan so the shrimp cook evenly.
cooking_steps: Bring the coconut cream to a lively boil in a wide pan over high heat. Stir in the sugar and salt, then add the shrimp immediately and toss evenly.
Once the shrimp turn orange-red and are cooked through, lower the heat. Toss gently until the coconut cream reduces to a light glossy coating; stop before the pan becomes dry.
Serve hot with steamed rice. If using larger shrimp, check that the thickest flesh is fully cooked before turning off the heat.
tep-rang-dua-ben-tre.media_alt_text: A plate of silver shrimp stir-fried in coconut milk until orange and lightly glossy.
